title: Licences, permissions and restricted work
audience: Any worker in any home-service business in the academy, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Explain the boundary for licences, permissions and restricted work and identify when work must stop.
Prepare a task-specific, documented decision for licences, permissions and restricted work under company and local requirements.

instruction.heading: Why restricted work needs its own check
instruction.body: Some work that looks like cleaning is in fact regulated work. A worker who starts it without the right licence, permit or authorisation exposes themselves, the client and the business to legal and safety risk. This lesson teaches you to ask a set of questions before any task starts: does the work fall under a licensed trade, does it involve a regulated material or hazardous remediation, does the site require a permit or an approval from the owner or manager, and does your employer or insurer restrict the work? A yes to any of these means the task is restricted until it is cleared.

instruction.heading: Four sources of restriction
instruction.body: Restrictions come from four places. The first is licensing law: some trades and some equipment require a licence or certificate issued under state or territory rules, and each licence covers a defined class of work. The second is regulated materials: suspected asbestos-containing material, and other materials with specific removal rules, must not be disturbed by an unqualified worker. The third is site and owner permission: building managers, body corporates, tenants or clients may set their own rules for access, products, noise or specialised methods. The fourth is employer and insurer policy: your business may place certain tasks outside its approved scope even where the law would allow them. A single task can be restricted by more than one of these at once.

instruction.heading: Test the task before accepting it
instruction.body: Before accepting, describe the task in plain words, with the location, the materials and the method. Ask whether any part of it involves electrical wiring or fittings, gas, plumbing, structural change, roof or height access, the removal or disturbance of building materials, or a product or process that needs a special permit. Where the answer is yes or you are unsure, the task is restricted until you have checked the licence rules for the state or territory, the site owner's permission and your employer's written authority. Repairing electrical wiring is licensed work in New South Wales, where the licensing rules name repairing as part of electrical wiring work.

instruction.heading: Handle suspected asbestos correctly
instruction.body: A customer may ask a cleaner to remove a section of suspected asbestos-containing wall lining, or to dust, sand or scrape a surface that may contain it. Treat the material as hazardous until a competent person identifies it. Do not cut, scrape, sand, drill, sweep dry or otherwise disturb it, and do not carry out tests that would expose anyone to fibres. Keep other people out of the area, record what you saw and what the client reported, and refer the work to an appropriately authorised provider.

instruction.heading: Confirm permission with the person who holds it
instruction.body: A permission is valid only when the person who has authority gives it in writing and it covers the exact task, location and method. A client's verbal agreement does not authorise restricted work, and neither does a colleague's assurance. Find out who controls the site, such as an owner, body corporate or facilities manager, and ask them to confirm access, working hours, any restricted products or methods, and any approval they need to give. Record the name, the date and the scope of the permission before work starts.

instruction.heading: What a training certificate does and does not do
instruction.body: A training certificate shows that a person completed a course on a topic. On its own it does not grant a licence, permit or authority, and it does not show that the holder is currently competent for a specific task. Before a restricted task starts, check that the required licence is current and covers the work, that the employer or site has authorised the task in writing, and that a competent person has verified the worker's skills for the method being used. This lesson gives you the decision steps. It does not grant any authority.

instruction.heading: Licence notice
instruction.body: Licence notice: This lesson does not grant the right to perform any licensed, permitted or restricted work, and it does not make the learner a licence holder. A high risk work licence for boom-type elevating work platforms applies where the boom is 11 metres or more in New South Wales and Queensland, so a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold. Work above ground level from ladders, scaffolds or platforms is restricted and needs your employer's written authorisation, and the licence rules where you work must be checked before it starts.

instruction.heading: Stop-work rule
instruction.body: Stop, make the area safe and tell your supervisor before resuming if the task needs a licence, permit or authority you do not hold, if a client or colleague asks you to start before permission is in writing, if you find or suspect a regulated material such as asbestos-containing material, if a licensed system such as electrical wiring is involved, or if the task changes after you have been briefed. Keep people away from the area and do not resume until the decision-maker has given written approval.

procedure: Describe the task in plain words, with the location, the materials, the method and any height or access involved.
Ask whether the task involves licensed trade work, a regulated material, height access, a site-owner permit or an employer restriction.
Where the answer is yes or unsure, mark the task restricted and place it on hold.
Check the licence rules for the state or territory, and list any points still to be checked for the decision-maker.
Obtain written permission from the site owner or manager, and written authorisation from your employer, for the exact task.
Confirm that any required licence is current, covers the work and is held by the person who will do it.
If the task is outside the permitted scope, refer it to an appropriately authorised provider and tell the client in writing what was excluded.
Record the decision, the approver, the permissions obtained and the conditions for resuming in the job record.

workedExamples.situation: A customer asks a cleaner to remove a section of suspected asbestos-containing wall lining.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the first safe action, and who must be told?
workedExamples.reasoning: The first safe action is to stop, keep people away from the area and avoid disturbing the material. Removal is regulated work, and a cleaning booking does not authorise it. Tell the customer that removal is excluded and refer it to an appropriately authorised provider. Record what was observed, what the customer reported and who was told. Do not take samples or run tests that would expose anyone to fibres.

workedExamples.situation: A client adds an electrical wiring repair to the cleaning request.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Can the cleaner add the repair to the job?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. The cleaner removes the repair from the job, tells the client it is outside the cleaning scope and recommends a licensed electrician. The cleaner does not open the fitting or test it, and records the request and the client's response. The cleaning booking is not permission for any electrical work.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence notice: completing this lesson is not a licence, certificate or authority to do regulated or restricted work. Check the licence or authorisation rules for your state or territory, and obtain your employer or site written authorisation before starting any work that is outside your training.

Stop-work rule: stop, make the area safe and tell your supervisor before continuing if the task is outside your training or authorisation, the hazard or the required permission is unclear, or the client asks for work that the work order does not cover.

qualityStandard: Each task is checked for licensed trade work, regulated materials, height access, site permits and employer restrictions before it starts.
A task with a yes or unsure answer is held as restricted until it is cleared.
Permission is given in writing by the person with authority and covers the exact task, location and method.
Suspected asbestos-containing material is not disturbed, and its removal is referred to an authorised provider.
summary: Check every task for licensed trade work, regulated materials, height access, site permits and employer restrictions before it starts.
Treat a task as restricted when the answer is yes or unsure, and place it on hold.
Permission must be given in writing by the person with authority, and must cover the exact task.
A training certificate does not grant a licence, permit or authority.
A cleaner does not disturb suspected asbestos-containing material; removal is referred to an appropriately authorised provider.

knowledgeChecks.question: Before starting work classified as "Licences, permissions and restricted work", what must you do?
options: Identify task-specific unknown hazards, qualifications, permissions and controls; place work on hold until verified.
Start the work and check hazards as you go, since the client has asked for it and the client has paid a deposit
Accept the task if your past experience with similar jobs was safe and the client has been clear about what they want
Ask the client to sign a waiver so the work can begin and the waiver covers every hazard on site

knowledgeChecks.question: Can you start restricted work on the strength of a training certificate alone?
options: Yes, once the employer signs off the training certificate and the client has agreed to the job
No. Relevant licences, employer/site authorisation and independent competence verification remain required.
Yes, if the client agrees in writing and the client pays a deposit up front for the job
Only if the work is outdoors and at ground level and the work is short, simple and low risk

knowledgeChecks.question: What does the lesson say about work that looks like cleaning?
options: Some of it is regulated work
